name: Wakidani no Tochinoki

location.address: Wakidani, Kurigata, Toga, Nanto, Toyama Prefecture

transport: Roughly one hour by car from the Tonami Interchange on the Hokuriku Expressway; the Toga district of Nanto City is rural mountain country.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree, one of Japan's largest horse chestnuts. Designated National Natural Monument on 20 October 1926. Traditional accounts give roughly 1,000 years; the current scientific estimate is closer to 800 years, so age_estimate uses the more conservative figure. Girth roughly 11.8m at the wider ground level (9.7m measured 1.5m higher), unusually smooth-barked for an old tochinoki, which typically develops heavy knotting. Trunk interior is partly hollow, and two major branches broke off in heavy-snow winters, 1981 and 1988, visibly reducing the crown and vigor since. Still alive and standing today per the most recent description found, but the story should say plainly that this is a diminished giant rather than a pristine one. No fresh (post-2020) health survey found; flagged for that gap as well as for the traditional-vs-scientific age discrepancy.
